course_name_original: Control y Protección de Máquinas Eléctricas
course_name_en: Control and Protection of Electrical Machines

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write, develop, and manage industrial engineering projects involving the installation, assembly, and operation of industrial control and protection systems for machines.

Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations in the field of control and protection of electrical machines.
Ability to solve problems on control and protection of electrical machines with initiative, creativity, and critical reasoning.

Ability to perform measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks in the field of control and protection of electrical machines.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards in the field of control and protection of electrical machines.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to prevent occupational risks and protect the health and safety of workers and users in the field of electrical machines.
Ability to act with honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines, applied to the control and protection of electrical machines.
Knowledge of the fundamentals and control methods applied to the operation control of electrical machines.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Knowledge of the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

Knowledge of the basic principles of control and protection of electrical machines that will facilitate the learning of currently used systems and adaptation to new systems that may arise in the future, in the field of control and protection of electrical machines.
Knowledge of the principles of automatic regulation and its application to industrial automation in the field of electrical machines.
Design and automate the operation of electric motors, based on their electrical characteristics, using wired logic and programmed logic.
Select the appropriate variable speed drive based on its operating principle, and develop the structure and control strategies for specific industrial applications using electric motors.
Identify incidents that can affect the correct functioning of electrical machines, as well as the detectors and protections available on the market.
Choose and calculate the appropriate protection for various electrical machines based on their power, use, type of incident, and the circumstances surrounding an electrical installation.
Write and present a technical report on the application of acquired knowledge on control and protection of electrical machines.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to electric drives
Examples of electric drives in industry
Theory of space vectors in three-phase systems
Introduction to space vectors
Space vectors in three-phase systems: mathematical and graphical description
Reference systems: Park transform
Air gap flux space vector and induced voltage
Vectorial PWM
Dynamic description of three-phase R-L systems
General dynamic scheme of three-phase machines
General equation of torque production
Dynamic modeling of rotary electrical machines
Introduction to dynamic modeling
Dynamic model of the induction machine
Dynamic model of the synchronous machine
Dynamic model of the permanent magnet machine
Dynamic model of the reluctance machine
Control of power converters
General structure of control schemes
Volts/Hz control of AC drives
Vector control of AC drives
Vector control of the induction motor: direct and indirect control
Vector control of the induction generator: DFIG (wind turbines)
Vector control of the synchronous motor
Vector control of the permanent magnet synchronous motor
Vector control of the reluctance synchronous motor
Use of DSP for control implementation. A/D converters. Digital inputs/outputs. Interrupts
Current measurement: current sensors, signal adaptation, resolution, sensor selection
Speed measurement: the encoder as an element for measuring speed and position. Types. Schemes. Operation
Design of vectorial regulators
Simplified models of machines with current control
Inverter modeling
PID schemes in dq axes
Design of I/V decoupling regulators. Design examples
Current/speed/position control
Introduction to current/speed/position control
Current/speed/position control of the induction motor
Current/speed/position control of the synchronous motor
Current/speed/position control of the permanent magnet synchronous motor
Current/speed/position control of the reluctance motor
Selection of the appropriate drive-machine set
Introduction to drive selection
Factors for choosing a drive
Protection of machines and drives
Introduction to protection
Protection of electrical machines
Protection of electrical drives
Development of a drive for an induction motor
Implement the dynamic model (Topics 2 and 3)
Control in a DSP (Topics 4 and 5)
Perform current/speed control (Topic 6)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (test / development questions / problem solving)
Delivery of 2 tasks: testing different control strategies in laboratory trainer. Signal measurement.
Public presentation of developed drive projects
Attitude, participation and completion of laboratory practices

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated based on four components: a written exam (30%), two tasks testing control strategies and signal measurement (20%), a public presentation of projects (40%), and evaluation of attitude, participation, and laboratory practices (10%). Attendance to laboratory practices is mandatory for evaluation. The sum of the weights is 10 points.
